steps.title: Start at the cortical target
steps.claim: The coil is positioned over left DLPFC. “DLPFC” covers a broad cortical region; the precise stimulation site varies across targeting approaches.
steps.displayLimit: Left middle-frontal parcels approximate DLPFC; no coil field is shown.

steps.title: Connect the target to sgACC
steps.claim: Fox and Weigand linked antidepressant response to the functional relationship between the stimulation site and sgACC. More negative resting-state connectivity was associated with better response.
steps.displayLimit: The dashed line is functional. Left-side sgACC is an orientation surface, not the reported seed location. No direct DLPFC–sgACC fiber is drawn.

steps.title: Keep the deep circuit in view
steps.claim: Prefrontal stimulation can affect deeper structures. A TMS–PET experiment in healthy volunteers found a dopamine response in the ipsilateral caudate. The atlas’s corticostriatal tract gives this relationship anatomical context.
steps.displayLimit: The displayed tract is a whole reference bundle, not a patient’s stimulated fibers.

steps.title: Carry the right explanation into clinic
steps.claim: DLPFC TMS is a cortical intervention with network effects. Functional targeting studies support the sgACC relationship, while the exact anatomical routes and causal mechanisms require additional evidence.
steps.locator: Conclusions; interpretation of the cited studies
steps.displayLimit: No treatment strength, direction of electrical flow, or individual response is encoded.

connections.label: Functional anticorrelation
connections.description: Better outcomes were associated with more negative resting-state connectivity between the stimulated DLPFC site and sgACC. This relationship does not identify a direct fiber or establish a complete treatment mechanism.

connections.label: Frontostriatal context
connections.description: Reference corticostriatal fibers supply anatomical context. Healthy-volunteer TMS–PET supports a downstream caudate effect, not proof that this bundle mediates depression improvement.

steps.title: Locate the cortical entry point
steps.claim: Carmi’s H7 deep-TMS protocol targeted medial prefrontal/anterior cingulate circuitry and paired treatment with individualized symptom provocation.
steps.displayLimit: A medial cortical approximation is shown, not an H7 field or isolated direct ACC stimulation.

steps.title: Reveal the deep partners
steps.claim: The rationale involves frontal–striatal–thalamic circuitry. These deep partners help explain the choice of cortical territory even though the coil is outside the skull.
steps.displayLimit: Only two circuit arms are shown. Pallidal relays and a complete synaptic loop are omitted.

steps.title: Separate the rationale from the trial result
steps.claim: The randomized trial reported more OCD responders with active than sham treatment. This supports the tested protocol; it does not determine which individual tract carried the benefit.
steps.locator: Results; 38.1% versus 11.1% post-treatment response among assessed participants
steps.displayLimit: Reference bundles are shown; no trial-specific stimulated fibers are available.

steps.title: Distinguish neighboring cortical approaches
steps.claim: Pre-SMA and dmPFC approaches use different targets and protocols. They should be taught separately from the H7 medial-prefrontal/ACC approach. Open the pre-SMA lesson to follow its STN connection.
steps.displayLimit: Left hemisphere is isolated to show the medial surface; it does not imply unilateral H7 treatment.

connections.label: Corticostriatal arm
connections.description: A selected arm of the circuit motivating the H7 protocol. The study tested a treatment protocol, not selective activation of this displayed fiber bundle.

connections.label: Thalamocortical arm
connections.description: The thalamic relationship supplies broader circuit context. Intermediate basal-ganglia relays are omitted; this drawing is not a complete closed loop.

lessons.question: Why connect pre-SMA to the STN?

steps.title: Start at pre-SMA
steps.claim: Pre-SMA is a medial frontal action-control region, posterior to the dmPFC approach. Ji’s OCD trial stimulated an individually selected right pre-SMA site.
steps.displayLimit: An anterior-SMA anatomical estimate is shown, not Ji’s individual target.

steps.title: Add striatum and STN
steps.claim: Pre-SMA participates in striatal and subthalamic circuitry. The striatal arm and the STN-linked targeting relationship are distinct connections, shown with different line styles.
steps.displayLimit: The pre-SMA–STN 3D subset is an anatomical estimate with asymmetric source coverage.

steps.title: Understand the targeting experiment
steps.claim: In a randomized study of 37 people, Ji used STN connectivity to choose the cortical target. Active treatment improved OCD symptoms more than sham, with associated changes in the functional target network.
steps.locator: Abstract; Results; clinical and connectivity analyses
steps.displayLimit: One small trial does not establish this pathway as the universal mediator of OCD TMS.

steps.title: Keep the evidence proportional
steps.claim: Pre-SMA studies differ in laterality and targeting. Mantovani used bilateral stimulation; Fitzsimmons used left pre-SMA in a different protocol. The right-sided example here belongs specifically to Ji.
steps.displayLimit: The right-side display follows Ji’s target; it is not a claim of right-hemisphere superiority.

connections.label: Striatal connection
connections.description: Anatomical work places pre-SMA in associative striatal circuitry. The superior corticostriatal bundle is broad reference anatomy.

connections.label: STN-linked targeting
connections.description: Ji selected a right pre-SMA TMS site using individual STN functional connectivity. The separate 3D hyperdirect-pathway estimate is population anatomy, not the study’s targeting map.

lessons.question: Why does the DBS location matter?

steps.title: Locate the white-matter corridor
steps.claim: Capsular DBS places contacts near multiple fiber populations. The ventral capsule and neighboring ventral striatum are close together, so the broad target label alone does not specify the stimulated network.
steps.displayLimit: The whole internal capsule provides orientation. It does not delineate vALIC or a stimulation volume.

steps.title: Follow the ventral-capsule network
steps.claim: In Tyagi’s six-person comparison, effective ventral-capsule stimulation connected predominantly with medial OFC. VC stimulation had a stronger mood effect than amSTN stimulation.
steps.displayLimit: General capsular bundles provide context; the study-specific medial OFC pathway is not reconstructed.

steps.title: Compare the subthalamic entry point
steps.claim: The amSTN-connected network included lateral OFC, dACC and DLPFC. Both DBS sites reduced OCD symptoms; improved cognitive flexibility was found with amSTN stimulation.
steps.locator: Results: Tractography and cognitive flexibility; Figure 3
steps.displayLimit: The whole STN and population pathways are shown; the precise amSTN treatment volume is unavailable.

steps.title: Zoom from target names to contacts
steps.claim: Tyagi reported the most effective contacts at the dorsal end of the VC/VS lead and the deepest end of the amSTN lead. The contact comparison shows a separate published example of different acute experiences at adjacent contacts.
steps.locator: Tyagi Results: active contacts; Tsai Results/Table 2
steps.displayLimit: No “contact 4” rule is inferred. Contact numbering and implanted trajectories vary.

connections.label: VC-connected network
connections.description: Effective ventral-capsule stimulation volumes were linked predominantly with medial OFC in Tyagi’s tractography analysis.

connections.label: amSTN-connected network
connections.description: Tractography associated the effective amSTN site with lateral OFC, dACC and DLPFC. The diagram omits dACC to keep this comparison compact.

connections.label: Prefrontal connection
connections.description: DLPFC was among the cortical destinations from the effective amSTN stimulation volume. Reference STN pathways are not those individual treatment fibers.

steps.title: Distinguish cortex from white matter
steps.claim: SCC DBS targets white matter beside the subgenual cingulate cortex. The nearby sgACC helps orient us, but a cortical surface is not the DBS stimulation site.
steps.displayLimit: The precise SCC white-matter target has no boundary mask in this atlas.

steps.title: Reveal the converging fiber systems
steps.claim: Riva-Posse’s work associated response with pathways toward medial frontal, cingulate and subcortical destinations. Prospective targeting sought convergence of four fiber systems: forceps minor, uncinate, cingulum and frontostriatal fibers.
steps.displayLimit: Reference bundles are shown. Their visual overlap does not define a validated stimulation sweet spot.

steps.title: Understand the evidence for targeting
steps.claim: A prospective open-label cohort used tractography to guide targeting. Its encouraging outcomes support further study of this approach, while the absence of a sham comparison limits causal interpretation.
steps.displayLimit: The 3D anatomy does not reproduce the cohort’s electrodes or activation volumes.

steps.title: Include the controlled result
steps.claim: The larger Holtzheimer sham-controlled SCC trial did not find a significant active-versus-sham benefit during the blinded phase. A compelling circuit model does not erase that result.
steps.locator: Holtzheimer abstract: primary blinded comparison; Riva-Posse cohort
steps.displayLimit: The left medial view is for visibility; these DBS studies used bilateral implantation.

connections.label: Forceps minor / uncinate
connections.description: SCC responder tractography included medial frontal connections through forceps minor and uncinate. These are two distinct fiber systems.

connections.label: Cingulum
connections.description: Cingulum pathways connect the SCC region with rostral and dorsal cingulate territories.

connections.label: Descending connections
connections.description: Subcortical connections were part of responder tractography. The displayed corticostriatal bundle is contextual, not a complete reconstruction of the study’s descending paths.

contactCase.title: One lead, different immediate experiences
contactCase.setting: Reported test: 6 V · 210 μs · 130 Hz · monopolar
contactCase.description: Compare adjacent contacts 1 and 2. Both elicited smiling/laughter, but reported euphoria differed. These are observations in one person, not a prediction for another patient.

contacts.title: Deepest contact
contacts.detail: At 6 V, the report describes smile/laughter with euphoria. Smell and chest tightness were also reported.
contacts.locator: Results: Psychiatric responses; Table 2, case 1, contact 0

contacts.title: Second from the tip
contacts.detail: At 6 V, smile/laughter was accompanied by reported euphoria. The table also lists smell, chest tightness and increased sexual drive at this voltage.
contacts.locator: Results: Psychiatric responses; Table 2, case 1, contact 1

contacts.title: Third from the tip
contacts.detail: At 6 V, smile/laughter occurred without reported euphoria. Smell, chest tightness and increased sexual drive were also listed at this voltage.
contacts.locator: Results: Psychiatric responses; Table 2, case 1, contact 2

contacts.title: Most superficial contact
contacts.detail: Table 2 lists no smile/laughter response for this contact across the tested voltages. Smell was reported at 6 V. The text does not supply an exact euphoria rating for this contact at 6 V.
contacts.locator: Table 2, case 1, contact 3; no individual euphoria score inferred from the group figure

contactCase.limits: The lead drawing preserves nominal contact dimensions. It is not implanted into the atlas: the study does not supply a matched patient tractogram or a validated tract assignment for these individual responses. No activation volume is estimated.
contactCase.takeaway: A smile, a subjective mood change, and sustained improvement in OCD are different outcomes. Nearby contacts can differ, and the contact number alone is not an anatomical label.
